newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Lower House passes extra budget for 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan Lower House passes extra budget for 96/97.

text.p: Japan's Lower House of parliament on Wednesday approved a supplementary budget totalling 2.67 trillion yen for the 1996/97 fiscal year ending March 31.

The three opposition parties had called for revisions to the budget including changes in its priorities and reductions in some spending, but the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) refused to accept the demands.
The LDP passed the extra budget with the help of two parties with which it has formed a loose policy alliance.
The Upper House is expected to start debate on the extra budget on Thursday.
The extra budget will fund the rehabilitation of areas around Kobe in western Japan, hit by a massive earthquake in 1995, and measures to help cope with natural disasters.

It will also cover the costs of a serious food poisoning outbreak during the summer and measures taken to cushion farmers after a global trade agreement in 1993 liberalised farm trade. The budget also includes provisions related to the scaling back of U.S. military bases in Okinawa.
The government plans to issue about 1.34 trillion yen worth of bonds to fund the extra budget.
